Title: QR Code Scanner
Description: Read a QR code with your camera or from a PNG, JPEG or WebP image in the browser, then copy the text or open http(s) links. Nothing is uploaded.
Keywords: QR code scanner, QR scanner camera, read QR code from image, QR code decoder, scan QR from screenshot, scan QR code with webcam, decode QR code online
DropZone: Drag & drop an image with a QR code here
ErrorReading: Error reading text from the image.
ErrorNoQr: No QR code found in the image. Please try another image.
ErrorUnsupportedImage: Unsupported image format. Use PNG, JPEG or WebP.
ErrorCopy: Could not copy to the clipboard.
Seo_Introduction: Read a QR code with your device camera or from a screenshot or photo: the decoded text appears ready to copy, and links get an Open Link button. Everything is decoded locally in your browser.
Seo_DetailedDescription:
PNG, JPEG and WebP images are supported; GIF and other formats get an error message. Decoding uses rxing, a Rust port of ZXing compiled to WebAssembly, inside a Web Worker, so even a photo of about 3800 px does not freeze the page, and choosing another file cancels the previous scan.

**Scan with camera** opens the rear camera with a framing guide; when the device has several cameras, a **Camera** list lets you switch. Frames are downscaled to at most 1024 px and decoded in the same Web Worker, and a new frame is taken only after the previous one is finished, so the page stays smooth. Scanning stops at the first code found (**Scan again** restarts it), and the camera is switched off on **Stop camera**, when the tab is hidden or when you upload a file. The camera needs HTTPS (or localhost) and your permission; frames are processed on the device and never sent anywhere.

The full payload is shown as text: URLs, plain text, Wi-Fi strings, contact cards, Unicode and emoji. Only http and https links get **Open Link**; other schemes such as `javascript:` are never turned into links. If no code is found, try a sharper image in which the whole code and its white border are visible.
Seo_Examples:
**Link from a screenshot**: a PNG made with QR Code Generator for `https://example.com/path?q=1` shows that URL and an **Open Link** button.

**Camera**: click **Scan with camera**, allow access and hold a printed code inside the frame — the text appears in under a second and the camera turns off.

**Large photo**: a 3848×3848 px JPEG decodes in about 1–1.5 seconds on a desktop while the page stays responsive.

**No code in the picture**: you get “No QR code found in the image. Please try another image.”
Seo_HowToSteps:
### Step 1: Choose an image or start the camera
Click **Choose file** or drop a PNG, JPEG or WebP image onto the zone — or click **Scan with camera** and allow camera access.

### Step 2: Read the result
An image is decoded automatically; with the camera, point it at the code until it is recognized. The text appears under **Scanned Content**.

### Step 3: Use the content
Click **Copy**, or **Open Link** for an http(s) address. Use **Scan again** to read the next code with the camera.
Seo_Tips:
- Crop loosely: keep the whole code and some white margin around it in the picture or camera frame.
- Avoid glare and motion blur on photos of screens or printed codes; hold the phone steady for a moment.
- If the camera is blocked, allow it in the browser's site settings; on a page without HTTPS the camera is unavailable, so upload an image instead.
- Inverted (light on dark) or very low-contrast codes may not be found.
- Check the shown address before clicking **Open Link** — QR codes are a common way to hide phishing links.
